pr_title: Use min_size/max_size to limit window size and position while popup center
pr_body:
<!--
Pull requests should always be made for the `master` branch first, as that's
where development happens and the source of all future stable release branches.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed.

Do not create a pull request for stable branches unless the change is already
available in the `master` branch and it cannot be easily cherry-picked.
Alternatively, if the change is only relevant for that branch (e.g. rendering
fixes for the 3.2 branch).
-->


Fix #62163.

The `popup_center*` methods need to determine the popup position according to the actual size of the window.

Previously, `max_size`/`min_size` was not considered in these methods, which in some cases could cause the window to actually be off-center.

In this PR, Add a method to get the minimum size of content that has been clamped by a custom minimum size. `Window::get_clamped_minimum_size`.

`min_size` will be considered in `Window::get_clamped_minimum_size`. The result is to return the value clamped by the custom min size.

And `wrap_controls` is also taken into account. if `wrap_controls` is not enabled, `Window::get_clamped_minimum_size` return `min_size` directly.

The return value of `get_clamped_minimum_size` is the actual **lower** limit of the window `size`, and `max_size` is the actual **upper** limit of the window `size`.

~~If a component of `max_size` is `0`, it means there is no limit on the corresponding axis. This is the same as before.~~

Follow the rules of `min_size`/`max_size`, but at this stage `max_size` seems to be unable to limit only one axis when resize, and let the other axis unlimited. Only `(0, 0)` means unlimited, a single component of `0` is not yet possible, it may only invalidate the entire `max_size`. Therefore, for consistency, `max_size` will use the same invalidation rules as in #63925.

Edit:

| Control | Window | Explanation |
| :--------: | :---------: | :--------------: |
| `get_custom_minimum_size` | `get_min_size` | Get custom min size limit |
| `get_minimum_size` | `get_contents_minimum_size` | Get contents minimum size |
| `get_combined_minimum_size` | `get_clamped_minimum_size` | Get the minimum size of the content that has been clamped by the custom min size |

| Before | After | Explanation |
| :-------: | :-----: | :-------------: |
| ![0](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/190615521-fd91e856-d467-4fc9-84a1-848de0ec3312.gif) | ![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/190615544-afc010e6-9464-4d6c-ad82-f14fcf251dcd.gif) | `max_size = (300, 200)` |
| ![3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/190615659-908074f2-b808-407a-b94f-6789705a1d9c.gif) | ![2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30386067/190615687-d4e2500e-9d50-44e1-9c69-47fbe26a1ab6.gif) | `max_size = (0, 0)` or **invalid** (eg. `max_size = (300, 200)`; `min_size = (0, 300)`)

issue_context.title: When popup center, non-default limit value will make the window off-center
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.alpha9.official [fc18891db]

### System information

Linux Mint 20.3, Vulkan, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti

### Issue description

If `max_size`/`min_size` is not `(0,0)` (the default value), the window may be off-center when calling `pop_center`. ~~It may be caused by not considering these two limit values when calculating `_get_contents_minimum_size`.~~ 

I'm not sure if these limits should be considered in `_get_contents_minimum_size`, in `AcceptDialog`, only `min_size.x` is considered, in other `Window` derived classes, these are not considered at all. Probably because of `wrap_controls` (it seems redundant in AcceptDialog), `_get_contents_minimum_size` is calculated completely differently in `Window` and `AcceptDialog`. Maybe we should also take `wrap_controls` into account when calculating.

### Steps to reproduce

Make `max_size` small enough or make `min_size` large enough before calling `popup_center()`

### Minimal reproduction project

[popup-center-off-center.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10670922/popup-center-off-center.zip)

review_comments: You should keep this comment and also include a note about clamping.

This PR indirectly limits the size:

1. Make `min_size` and `max_size` follow the size limit of the rendering server, see `Window::_clamp_limit_size()`;
2. Then make sure that `max_size_used` is not less than `min_size`, see `Window::_validate_limit_size()`.

`max_size_used` is the upper limit of actual use, it will be clamped by `min_size` and `max_size`, combined with 1, it will eventually follow the size limit of the rendering server.

`get_clamped_minimum_size()` returns the actual lower bound used, which takes into account the case when `wrap_controls` is enabled.

>     2. Then make sure that `max_size_used` is not less than `min_size`, see `Window::_validate_limit_size()`.

It just ensures that when `max_size` is not as large as `min_size`, `RS::get_singleton()->get_maximum_viewport_size()` is actually used. I'm not sure whether this method returns `(0,0)`.
Since this is not an obvious functionality, I believe, that it should be documented in a comment.
OK, some comments have been added.
This is the minimum window size can actually reach, it may be larger than `min_size` when `wrap_controls` is enabled.
